279 projects

As of August 2026 · changes weekly — re-check before citing

A working set of identified proposals a community can track, not a census — most of the country's activity is not in here yet. Pennsylvania is the exception: its rows are synced from PA DEP's own data-center permit tracker, so the state's coverage is close to complete and carries the permit trail with it. **Each row carries its own provenance.** Rows showing a verification date link to reporting or the governing body's own record and were read on that date; rows marked *unverified* have no source on record — a lead to check, not a fact to cite. **Stage is derived, not asserted.** *Hearing scheduled*, *Awaiting decision*, *Approved* and *Withdrawn* are computed from each row's milestone dates on every rebuild, so a hearing date that has passed stops reading 'scheduled'. Hearings get moved and projects re-file under new names — treat a scheduled date as the earliest to act by, and confirm with the clerk before relying on it. Leads are mined into data/project_candidates.json and promoted here only after a human reads a primary source.

Project dossiers

The full record for each project, with ownership, the next thing to do, and the sourced timeline of what has happened so far.

Dickerson Data Center Campus (Atmosphere) Hearing scheduled

Dickerson (Montgomery County), MD · 110 ac · Operator: Atmosphere Data Centers

Atmosphere Data Centers (which took over the project from Terra Innovations, whose initial conditional-use application dates to January 2024) proposes a five-building data center campus on 110 acres at the decommissioned Dickerson Generating Station coal plant site; a major modification to the conditional use was filed in December 2025 and amended plans are on Montgomery Planning's development database. On 2026-07-28 the Montgomery County Council approved an 18-month moratorium on new data center approvals that encompasses this proposal; Office of Zoning and Administrative Appeals hearings had been scheduled for Sept 10-11, 2026.

Next step: Public hearing in 4 days (2026-09-10). Sign up to speak and file written comment before then.

Source

Find the paper trail (0 filed · 11 places to look)

State environmental permits

Backup generators, water withdrawal and stormwater are permitted by the state, usually earlier and in more detail than anything filed locally.

  • Maryland Dept. of the EnvironmentThe program page: which permits this state requires, and the office that issues them.
  • Search Maryland Dept. of the Environment for this projectsearchThis state publishes no searchable permit database, so a written records request to the agency is the reliable route. Use this search only to find the right office.

County & town filings

The rezoning application, site plan, traffic and noise studies, staff report and every revision.

  • Search Dickerson (Montgomery County) planning filingssearchPlanning departments post application files under many different names. Find the department, then ask the clerk for the application number — that number unlocks everything else.
  • Search Dickerson (Montgomery County) property records / GISsearchThe parcel record names the buying LLC and the sale date, which is what ties an anonymous filing to an operator.

Utility & grid records

The electricity request is filed with the grid operator and the utility long before the town hears about it — and states the real load.

  • PJM Interconnection (Mid-Atlantic, Ohio Valley) — interconnection queueRequested megawatts, queue position and target in-service date. The MW here is the real number; the one at the town meeting is often phase one.
  • Maryland Public Service Commission — docket searchSpecial contracts, large-load tariffs and rate cases are docketed here. Testimony and exhibits are public, and are usually more candid than the press release.
  • FERC eLibraryFederal filings: transmission agreements, interconnection service agreements, and co-location disputes.
  • Search the serving utility for a will-serve lettersearchThe will-serve or load-service letter is the utility's own written commitment. Ask the utility and the PUC for it by name — it is frequently the first document to exist.

Federal databases

Works anywhere, and covers the operator's record at its other sites.

  • EPA ECHO facility searchEvery federally-reported air, water and waste permit at a facility, plus its inspection and violation history. Search by address or draw a radius around the site. This project's locality centres on 39.260, -77.420 — search that point with a 5-mile radius.
  • EPA EnvirofactsThe same underlying records, queryable by county — useful for 'what else is permitted near this site' rather than one facility.
  • EPA Facility Registry ServiceResolves the shell LLC on a permit to the facility it belongs to. Worth a look when the filing name means nothing locally.

These are places to look, not evidence that anything has been filed. Links were checked on 2026-08-21; search links are queries, not records. What to ask for.

900 Conshohocken Road data center (former Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill) Awaiting decision

Plymouth Township (Montgomery County), PA · 66 ac · Owner: Brian O'Neill (developer) · Filing LLC: 900 Conshohocken Road LLC

900 Conshohocken Road LLC, an entity of developer Brian O'Neill, seeks a special exception from Plymouth Township's zoning hearing board to convert the recently closed Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill — 10 existing buildings totaling about 2 million sq ft on 66 acres along the Schuylkill River — into a data center. The Aug. 6 hearing nearly filled a 750-seat auditorium; Conshohocken Borough was granted party status while Norristown was denied. The board set a procedural-only session for Aug. 17, with testimony continuing in September; an opposition petition has topped 4,000 signatures.

Next step: Heard 2026-08-17; decision pending. Call the board clerk for the vote date and get on the notification list.

Source
read 2026-08-14

Project Double Reed (Stream US Data Centers at STAMP) Awaiting decision

Alabama (Genesee County), NY · 600 MW · Operator: Stream Data Centers · Filing LLC: Stream US Data Centers LLC

Stream US Data Centers proposes a $19.46 billion, three-building, roughly 600 MW data center campus at the STAMP site in the Town of Alabama, Genesee County. The Town Planning Board reviewed site-plan conditions (annual noise monitoring, heat-island mitigation, a dedicated code enforcement officer) and was expected to vote July 6, but both July meetings were cancelled after GCEDC, the SEQRA lead agency, could not complete environmental-review documentation; the next scheduled Planning Board meeting was Aug 3, 2026. GCEDC's CEO says the project keeps moving unless New York's passed-but-unsigned statewide data center moratorium becomes law.

Backup generators, water withdrawal and stormwater are permitted by the state, usually earlier and in more detail than anything filed locally.

  • Wyoming DEQ — Air Quality DivisionThe program page: which permits this state requires, and the office that issues them.
  • Search Wyoming DEQ — Air Quality Division for this projectsearchThis state publishes no searchable permit database, so a written records request to the agency is the reliable route. Use this search only to find the right office.

County & town filings

The rezoning application, site plan, traffic and noise studies, staff report and every revision.

  • Search Wheatland (Platte County) planning filingssearchPlanning departments post application files under many different names. Find the department, then ask the clerk for the application number — that number unlocks everything else.
  • Search Wheatland (Platte County) property records / GISsearchThe parcel record names the buying LLC and the sale date, which is what ties an anonymous filing to an operator.

Utility & grid records

The electricity request is filed with the grid operator and the utility long before the town hears about it — and states the real load.

  • Southwest Power Pool (Plains) — interconnection queueRequested megawatts, queue position and target in-service date. The MW here is the real number; the one at the town meeting is often phase one.
  • Wyoming Public Service Commission — docket searchSpecial contracts, large-load tariffs and rate cases are docketed here. Testimony and exhibits are public, and are usually more candid than the press release.
  • FERC eLibraryFederal filings: transmission agreements, interconnection service agreements, and co-location disputes.
  • Search the serving utility for a will-serve lettersearchThe will-serve or load-service letter is the utility's own written commitment. Ask the utility and the PUC for it by name — it is frequently the first document to exist.

Federal databases

Works anywhere, and covers the operator's record at its other sites.

  • EPA ECHO facility searchEvery federally-reported air, water and waste permit at a facility, plus its inspection and violation history. Search by address or draw a radius around the site. This project's locality centres on 42.050, -104.950 — search that point with a 5-mile radius.
  • EPA EnvirofactsThe same underlying records, queryable by county — useful for 'what else is permitted near this site' rather than one facility.
  • EPA Facility Registry ServiceResolves the shell LLC on a permit to the facility it belongs to. Worth a look when the filing name means nothing locally.

These are places to look, not evidence that anything has been filed. Links were checked on 2026-08-21; search links are queries, not records. What to ask for.

Smithfield Gateway Data Center Awaiting decision

Smithfield Township (Monroe County), PA · — · Operator: DEPG Mosier Associates LP / DEPG of Shawnee II LP · Filing LLC: DEPG Mosier Associates LP

Two 250,000 sq ft data center buildings proposed at Smithfield Gateway behind St. Luke's and Wawa on Route 209. Developer filed a curative amendment application; township initiated a 180-day review period starting May 6, 2026. Township is proposing a new H-1 (Heavy Industrial) Zoning District where data centers would be the only permitted conditional use, removing them from ED and M-1 districts. Board of Supervisors held public hearing and vote on Aug 12, 2026.

Next step: Heard 2026-08-12; decision pending. Call the board clerk for the vote date and get on the notification list.

Stonebridge Associates data center campus at Powder Mill Works Awaiting decision

North Beaver & Mahoning townships (Lawrence County), PA · — · Operator: Stonebridge Associates

Maryland-based Stonebridge Associates has applied to build a data center campus at the Powder Mill Works commercial development site spanning North Beaver and Mahoning townships in Lawrence County, PA. The application was rejected administratively because a required $3,000 Lawrence County escrow check was missing, and back-to-back zoning hearings in early August 2026 argued over whether the application was validly filed - which determines whether older April or newer June zoning rules apply. The zoning board deferred its ruling, expected within 45 days.

Next step: Heard 2026-08-05; decision pending. Call the board clerk for the vote date and get on the notification list.

TeraWulf Cayuga data center (former Cayuga Power Plant) Awaiting decision

Lansing (Tompkins County), NY · 300 MW · Operator: TeraWulf

TeraWulf leases 183 acres of the 434-acre former Cayuga Power Plant site on Cayuga Lake in Lansing, NY, proposing ~125 acres of development: Phase 1 of 150 MW across three buildings plus a Phase 2 of another 150 MW. On April 27, 2026 the Lansing Planning Board deemed the site-plan application incomplete and requested lease details, construction-traffic data, and landscaping clarification; environmental groups' lawsuit over the Zoning Board's permit interpretation survived a standing challenge on April 29.

Next step: Heard 2026-04-27; decision pending. Call the board clerk for the vote date and get on the notification list.

Wolcott Data Center (Mid-America Commerce Park) Awaiting decision

White County, IN · 322 ac · Operator: Blue Ladder Development

Proposed data center at Mid-America Commerce Park, Wolcott, at the intersection of U.S. 24 and CR 1100 West. Site plans describe up to four data halls (~327,612 sq ft each), a 50,000 sq ft office building, and a 100,000 sq ft warehouse, with full build-out projected for 2029 and ~1,000 construction jobs over the build-out period; the developer's own site describes it as a 'closed-loop, minimal-water' campus seeking no incentives. Rezoning covers ~184 acres (per an Aug 2025 lawsuit) within a larger ~322-acre parcel. The rezoning applications were filed by the White County Redevelopment Commission rather than the property owners (BOWS4CRM and Liebengood Family Partnership) -- neighboring landowners Bart and Amy Snyder sued in Aug 2025 alleging the redevelopment commission lacked a notarized letter authorizing it to act as agent and that no site plan was submitted with the rezoning application, both allegedly required under White County's zoning ordinance. As of a June 2026 community open house, the project was still moving forward despite the moratorium and the pending lawsuit; White County Economic Development Organization President Randy Strasser confirmed the open house was authentic and co-hosted with the commissioners.

Next step: Heard 2025-08-11; decision pending. Call the board clerk for the vote date and get on the notification list.

  • 2026-01-01lawsuit

  • 2026-02-23announcement
    Gov. Landry and Amazon publicly announced a $12 billion, multi-site AWS data center buildout across Caddo and Bossier Parishes developed with STACK Infrastructure; expected to create 540 direct jobs and support 1,710 additional FTE positions. · source
  • 2026-02-23incentive
    Amazon detailed state incentives including LED FastStart workforce training, High Impact Jobs Program, Data Center Sales Tax Exemption, plus commitments to pay 100% of its own electricity costs and invest roughly $400 million in public water infrastructure. · source
  • 2026-02-23utility

  • 2026-02-25public-comment

  • 2026-03-01protest

  • 2026-03-18hearing

  • 2026-04-20ruling

  • 2026-07-13report

  • 2026-07-30public-comment

  • 2026-08-12coverage

  • 2026-08-17moratorium
    Commissioner John-Paul Young introduced Resolution 53 proposing a two-year moratorium on new data center developments, expansions, and tax incentive agreements in unincorporated Caddo Parish; would not affect the AWS campus already under construction. · source
  • 2026-08-18hearing

Amazon Bridgefield Tech Center (GW campus, Ashburn) In review

Ashburn (Loudoun County), VA · 122 ac · Operator: Amazon (AWS) · Owner: Amazon Data Services · Tenant: Amazon (AWS) · Filing LLC: Amazon Data Services

Four data center buildings (about 800,000 sq ft per WTOP; Northern Virginia Magazine reports ~400,000 sq ft plus three parking garages) on George Washington University's Virginia Science and Technology campus, filed as a site plan under 1972-era zoning so it would need no Planning Commission review, public hearing or Board vote. Andover HPC Data Center In review

Andover Township (Sussex County), NJ · 97 ac · Owner: National Land Developers · Filing LLC: Andover HPC Development

National Land Developers registered Andover HPC Development in December 2025 at 248 Stickles Pond Road, a 97-acre former airport site. Andover Township first allowed data centers in a redevelopment zone along Route 206 (September 2025) and raised the height limit to 65 feet (April 2026), but after a chaotic May 2026 meeting with 300 residents, the township passed Ordinance 2026-13 banning data centers township-wide. No formal site plan was ever filed. National Land Developers sued in Sussex County Superior Court on July 10, 2026, challenging the ban.

Next step: An application is in the record. Ask the planning office for the next hearing date and request formal notice.

  • 2026-01-01ruling

  • 2026-02-26coverage

  • 2026-05-03coverage
    Reporting revealed Google and Entergy were keeping the full terms of their energy rate contract sealed/confidential, raising transparency concerns among ratepayer advocates. · source
  • 2026-06-04financing
    Reporting detailed that bond issuances tied to the West Memphis Google data center PILOT financing could total as much as $60 billion in permanent financing authority over the deal 30-year term. · source
  • 2026-07-29public-comment
    At an Arkansas PSC hearing on Entergy proposed residential rate increase, speakers including the Little Rock NAACP chapter head cited the sealed Google contract as evidence of a lack of transparency. · source

Hexa Builders data center (Black Horse Pike) In review

Monroe Township (Gloucester County), NJ · — · Filing LLC: Hexa Builders LLC

Previously-approved warehouse project at 3043 South Black Horse Pike amended in early April 2026 to include a 1,000,000 sq ft data center. Two weeks later the township council stripped data-center permissions from the site and banned data centers township-wide; the planning board then deemed the amended application incomplete. Hexa is now suing the township for $300M+. Not dead - the litigation decides it.

Next step: Application filed. Ask the planning office for the hearing date and request formal notice.

Source
read 2026-08-07

Intelligence log (30 events)
  • 2019-09-23rezoning
    Monroe Township Council adopted Resolution R:221-2019, declaring the Commercial Corridor Rehabilitation Area along Black Horse Pike (Block 8401, Lots 8, 9, and 10, approximately 158 acres) an area in need of redevelopment. · source
  • 2023-02-01rezoning
    Monroe Township adopted Ordinance O:04-2023, approving the Hexa Builders Redevelopment Plan (revised November 15, 2022) permitting warehouse, storage, and distribution uses on the 158-acre site; data centers were not included as a permitted use. · source
  • 2023-03-16hearing
    The New Jersey Pinelands Commission published a public notice and scheduled a hearing on Monroe Township Ordinance O:04-2023 to determine whether the Hexa Builders Redevelopment Plan conformed with the Pinelands Comprehensive Management Plan. · source
  • 2025-03-12rezoning
    Monroe Township Council adopted Ordinance O:02-2025, amending the Hexa Builders Redevelopment Plan to add data centers and associated infrastructure (electrical systems, cooling equipment, network infrastructure, emissions control) as a permitted use. · source
  • 2025-12-23filing
    Residents within 200 feet of the Hexa Builders redevelopment site received certified mail notice of a January 8, 2026 planning board meeting regarding a 1.6-million-square-foot warehouse proposal at 3043 South Black Horse Pike. · source
  • 2026-01-08meeting
    At a January 8 Monroe Planning Board meeting, residents objected to the data center proposal, but the board approved Hexa's project that evening. · source
  • 2026-01-28vote
    On January 28 the Monroe Township Council directed the planning board to develop stricter data center standards, citing resident opposition. · source
  • 2026-02-02ruling
    On February 2 the Monroe Planning Board memorialized its approval of Hexa's project in a written resolution. · source
  • 2026-03-11meeting
    More than 100 residents packed a Monroe Township Council meeting lasting five hours; environmental groups including CRAN, Sustain South Jersey, Pinelands Alliance, and Food and Water Watch attended and raised concerns about the data center's water, energy, and noise impacts. · source
  • 2026-03-16announcement
    Mayor Gregory Wolfe announced in a Facebook video that a data center would not be coming to Monroe Township and that the council would remove data centers as a permitted use from the Hexa Redevelopment Plan at the March 25 meeting. · source
  • 2026-03-25vote
    At a March 25 council meeting, Monroe Township leaders heard resident concerns and approved a motion to change the ordinance so data centers could not be built in the community. · source
  • 2026-03-25filing
    Council introduced Ordinance O:20-2026 to eliminate data center use from the Hexa Builders Redevelopment Plan; all council members except John Valentine voted to introduce it, with Valentine wanting a broader ban and better public notification instead. · source
  • 2026-04-01filing
    Hexa Builders filed an amended application in early April 2026 converting one approved warehouse into a 1M sq ft data center at 3043 South Black Horse Pike. · source
  • 2026-04-08vote
    The Monroe Township council and ordinance committee voted to introduce a separate township-wide data center ban ordinance, with a final adoption vote scheduled for April 22. · source
  • 2026-04-22vote
    Township council passed two ordinances: one stripping data-center permissions from the specific site, the other banning data centers township-wide. · source
  • 2026-05-08coverage
    CBS Philadelphia reported on the ban, quoting Mayor Wolfe stating that Monroe Township has now banned any data center use from ever coming to the township. · source
  • 2026-05-12meeting
    Planning board unanimously deemed the amended site-plan application incomplete - blocking the project without rejecting it on the merits. · source
  • 2026-05-12ruling
    At the completeness review, township planner Christopher Dochney cited multiple application deficiencies including a missing environmental assessment, no Pinelands Certificate of Filing, unsigned plans, absent stormwater maintenance schedule, and incomplete electrical infrastructure documentation covering 3+ acres. · source
  • 2026-05-13operational
    Monroe Township's data center ban officially took effect on May 13. · source
  • 2026-05-13public-comment
    A coalition of 60 environmental, labor, and community organizations sent a letter to Governor Sherrill urging her to use emergency powers to impose a statewide moratorium on data centers consuming 20+ megawatts; Monroe Township resident Aleasha Whipple was quoted as a local organizer. · source
  • 2026-05-22hearing
    On May 22 Hexa presented its still-pending application, including the data center component, at a packed special planning board meeting attended by opposed residents. · source
  • 2026-06-05lawsuit
    On June 5 Hexa Builders filed a 104-page, 20-count lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court alleging First and 14th Amendment and state-law violations and seeking $300 million after Monroe denied its application. · source
  • 2026-07-06filing
    On July 6 the case was moved from New Jersey Superior Court to federal court in Camden; the Superior Court case closed. · source
  • 2026-07-09meeting
    At a July 9 planning board session, resident John Romano questioned how Hexa's application advanced and raised concerns about potential noise and pollution impacts on his property. · source
  • 2026-07-14hearing
    A case management conference was held in the Hexa Builders LLC and 3043 Williamstown Urban Renewal LLC v. Monroe Township case (Docket No. GLO-L-805-26). · source
  • 2026-07-17coverage
    Township Solicitor Sandra Graise stated the municipality is committed to vigorously and zealously defending the lawsuit while protecting residents' interests. · source
  • 2026-07-28filing
    On July 28 Monroe attorney Todd Gelfand filed a four-page letter seeking dismissal, arguing the ban does not regulate the content of speech, a speaker, a message, or the plaintiffs' ability to engage in expressive activity. · source
  • 2026-07-30ruling
    Hexa Builders sued Monroe Township for more than $300 million in damages over the ban and the completeness review. · source
  • 2026-08-01filing
    On August 1 Hexa's attorney Jim Maley asked the federal judge to reject Monroe Township's request to dismiss the lawsuit. · source
  • 2026-08-03filing
    Hexa attorney Jim Maley filed a letter requesting remand of the non-constitutional state-law claims back to New Jersey Superior Court, arguing state courts have more expertise on local land use laws. · source

Intelligence log (10 events)
  • 2023-11-07permit
    The Cheyenne Public Services Committee approved a development agreement for 'Project Cosmo,' a data center development by Goat Systems LLC on 945 acres in the High Plains Business Park. · source
  • 2024-05-09coverage
    As of this date Meta had not yet been publicly named as the company behind Project Cosmo/Goat Systems LLC, though Fortis Construction had roughly 800 workers on site clearing the 945-acre parcel and a public announcement was planned for early July 2024. · source
  • 2024-07-02announcement
    Meta formally announced its Cheyenne data center: an $800 million, 715,000-square-foot campus at High Plains Business Park expected to support about 100 jobs, with over 1,000 construction workers at peak and a 2027 online target, built by Fortis Construction with Black Hills Energy supplying grid resources. · source
  • 2025-05-26vote
    Cheyenne City Council voted 8-1 against a proposed 12-month moratorium on new data center development, after nearly four hours of public comment citing water supply, noise, farmland conversion, and pace-of-change concerns. · source
  • 2026-01-15environmental
    The Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities discovered white bacterial colonies during routine wastewater system testing, later traced to Meta's Cheyenne Data Center contractor. · source
  • 2026-02-23environmental
    The Wyoming Public Health Laboratory identified the bacteria found in Cheyenne's reclaimed water system as Cupriavidus gilardii, an unusual soil bacterium. · source
  • 2026-03-24environmental
    Investigators confirmed the same bacteria was present at Meta's predischarge storage tank, and Cheyenne's Board of Public Utilities revoked Goat Systems LLC's industrial discharge permit for the Meta data center. · source
  • 2026-06-26environmental
    The Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities issued its first public statement on the contamination, about four months after the bacteria was first discovered, citing the Meta data center operator for 'serious noncompliance' with wastewater discharge standards and a $10,000 fine. · source
  • 2026-07-02environmental
    The Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities announced it would stop accepting industrial wastewater from data-center fill-and-flush and closed-loop cooling operations citywide following the Meta contamination incident. · source
  • 2026-07-20lawsuit
    Meta/Goat Systems filed a six-page appeal disputing the source of the bacteria contamination, asking the Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities for a contested-case hearing and a refund of the $10,000 fine. · source

Intelligence log (19 events)
  • 2024-09-04protest
    Pennsylvania anti-nuclear activists began organizing to oppose the restart, citing safety and evacuation concerns tied to the 1979 TMI-2 accident. · source
  • 2024-09-20announcement
    Constellation Energy announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart the 835 MW Three Mile Island Unit 1, renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center, to supply carbon-free power for Microsoft data centers; the deal is expected to create ~3,400 jobs and add $16 billion to Pennsylvania GDP. · source
  • 2024-09-25coverage
    Local reporting captured mixed community reactions in Londonderry Township/Dauphin County, with labor groups voicing support while some residents raised fear of another accident. · source
  • 2024-10-25hearing
    Constellation laid out its reopening timeline at a public hearing, telling regulators and residents it aimed to have Unit 1 producing power again by 2027-2028. · source
  • 2024-11-04filing
    Constellation submitted its initial restart application to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission for Three Mile Island Unit 1 (Crane Clean Energy Center). · source
  • 2025-03-20environmental
    Constellation began evaluating the environmental impacts of the restart as part of the NRC review process, covering water use from the Susquehanna River, air quality, and spent fuel management. · source
  • 2025-04-03lawsuit
    Activist Gene Stilp sued Dauphin County commissioners and the Public Safety Department, alleging misuse of taxpayer funds to promote the plant restart. · source
  • 2025-05-06filing
    The NRC formally accepted Constellation restart request for Three Mile Island Unit 1 for detailed technical review. · source
  • 2025-08-01public-comment
    Residents told federal regulators the NRC review process feels like a charade, pressing concerns about safety, evacuation planning, and environmental impact at a public forum near the plant. · source
  • 2025-08-06hearing
    The NRC held a second public meeting, this one virtual, allowing community members nationwide to comment on the proposed restart of the Crane Clean Energy Center reactor. · source
  • 2025-08-15filing
    NRC staff issued a Request for Additional Information (RAI) to Constellation as part of the technical review of the Unit 1 restart application. · source
  • 2025-09-15filing

  • 2025-10-06filing

  • 2025-11-18financing

  • 2025-12-18coverage
    U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright touted the $1 billion DOE loan for the Three Mile Island restart as delivering on the Trump administration nuclear energy promises. · source
  • 2026-04-21filing

Monticello Tech data center campus In review

Monticello (Wright County), MN · 547 ac · Filing LLC: Monticello Tech

Monticello Tech, led by Frattalone Companies CEO Nick Frattalone, filed a land-use application with the City of Monticello, Minnesota on 2026-07-07 seeking rezoning to a Data Center Planned Unit Development district plus preliminary plat and conditional use permit approvals for a site south of 85th Street NE and east of Highway 25. The application describes 547 acres (364 developable), up to 3 million sq ft, as many as 8 principal buildings, about 75,000 gallons/day of water, and a connection to Xcel Energy's 345 kV system; the developer projects about $7 million in annual property tax at full buildout, with construction possibly starting Q1 2028. The eventual operator is not identified. City staff had until 2026-08-21 to determine whether the application is complete; Minnesota law then allows a 60-day review, extendable to 120 days.

Next step: Application filed. Ask the planning office for the hearing date and request formal notice.

Muncy Township Data Center In review

Muncy Township (Lycoming County), PA · — · Owner: DANKO Holdings II / Fishlips LLC · Filing LLC: Fishlips LLC

DANKO Holdings II / Fishlips LLC filed a zoning permit application on April 15, 2026, and a conditional use application on April 28, for three data center buildings along John Brady Drive near Yetter Road, about two miles east of the closed Lycoming Mall. The township failed to hold the required hearing within 60 days, and the developer published a legal notice in July claiming 'deemed approval' under the state Municipalities Planning Code. Supervisors imposed a nine-month moratorium on data center submissions in June 2026. The legal status of the deemed-approval claim is unresolved.

Next step: Application filed. Ask the planning office for the hearing date and request formal notice.

Mercer County / Burgin, KY · — · Operator: Panattoni Data Centers

Developer sought annexation into City of Burgin to escape Mercer County's one-year data center moratorium; residents cited environmental and utility-rate concerns.

Source

Intelligence log (13 events)
  • 2025-03-27incentive
    Kentucky enacted HB 775, expanding sales-and-use tax exemptions for qualified data centers statewide (effective July 1, 2025). · source
  • 2026-02-18public-comment
    Over 200 residents attended a Mercer County Joint Planning and Zoning Commission meeting, an early public airing of concerns about Project Bluegrass impact on farmland, wellbeing, and resource consumption. · source
  • 2026-07-09vote
    Burgin City Council voted 3-2 to advance a first reading of an ordinance to annex more than 1,000 acres of farmland, roughly doubling the city size, to enable Panattoni proposed hyperscale data center to bypass Mercer County zoning. · source
  • 2026-07-16vote
    Mercer County Fiscal Court voted to begin drafting an ordinance establishing a moratorium on new data center construction in the county. · source
  • 2026-07-20withdrawal
    Burgin canceled a scheduled special city council meeting on the annexation ordinance amid mounting public opposition and objections from neighboring Harrodsburg over water-supply capacity. · source
  • 2026-07-24public-comment
    Mercer County Joint Planning and Zoning Commission held a roughly two-hour public comment session on a proposed 17-page county data-center ordinance that would cap data-center zoning at 1,500 acres countywide. · source
  • 2026-07-30hearing
    Mercer County Fiscal Court gave first reading to the data-center moratorium ordinance; a related follow-up public meeting was held at Campbellsville University Harrodsburg Athletic Center. · source
  • 2026-08-06ruling
    Governor Andy Beshear signed Executive Order 2026-494, requiring data-center developers statewide to submit energy plans protecting ratepayers, pay their full share of taxes, and directing state agencies to deny permits causing negative environmental impacts. · source
  • 2026-08-12moratorium
    Mercer County Fiscal Court unanimously passed a one-year moratorium on new data-center applications in unincorporated parts of the county — a moratorium that would not apply if the project site is annexed into Burgin. · source
  • 2026-08-13public-comment
    Burgin City Council held its first public-comment session on the data center; 14 residents spoke against the project (an overflow room was needed) and the council deferred the annexation vote. · source
  • 2026-08-13report
    Reporting described Project Bluegrass as a proposed four-building, 900-acre data center campus up to 1,300 MW, with the developer claiming 1,500+ construction jobs, 100 permanent jobs, and $25-30 million in projected annual tax revenue for local schools. · source
  • 2026-08-17coverage
    Statewide public-radio reporting placed the Burgin/Mercer County fight in the context of more than a dozen Kentucky data-center proposals since the 2025 tax-incentive law, alongside moratoriums in Oldham County and Louisville Metro. · source
  • 2026-08-18coverage
    Kentucky Lantern analyzed whether Beshear data-center executive order has legal teeth absent enabling state legislation, in the context of the Burgin/Mercer County fight. · source

Project Bluestem In review

Tonganoxie (Leavenworth County), KS · 600 MW · Operator: Cloverleaf Infrastructure · Owner: Cloverleaf Infrastructure

Cloverleaf Infrastructure proposes Project Bluestem, a 600 MW hyperscale data center on approximately 1,000 acres of former Tailgate Ranch land south of Tonganoxie. The Leavenworth County Commission passed a 90-day moratorium on data center applications in May 2026, which expired in August. On August 5, commissioners voted 3-2 against extending the moratorium. On August 13, officials reversed course and directed planning and zoning to delay regulation recommendations until after a joint work session before the September meeting. No formal application has been submitted.

Next step: An application is in the record. Ask the planning office for the next hearing date and request formal notice.

State environmental permits

Backup generators, water withdrawal and stormwater are permitted by the state, usually earlier and in more detail than anything filed locally.

  • North Carolina DEQ — Division of Air QualityThe program page: which permits this state requires, and the office that issues them.
  • Search North Carolina DEQ — Division of Air Quality for this projectsearchThis state publishes no searchable permit database, so a written records request to the agency is the reliable route. Use this search only to find the right office.

County & town filings

The rezoning application, site plan, traffic and noise studies, staff report and every revision.

  • Search Walnut Cove (Stokes County) planning filingssearchPlanning departments post application files under many different names. Find the department, then ask the clerk for the application number — that number unlocks everything else.
  • Search Walnut Cove (Stokes County) property records / GISsearchThe parcel record names the buying LLC and the sale date, which is what ties an anonymous filing to an operator.

Utility & grid records

The electricity request is filed with the grid operator and the utility long before the town hears about it — and states the real load.

  • PJM Interconnection (Mid-Atlantic, Ohio Valley) — interconnection queueRequested megawatts, queue position and target in-service date. The MW here is the real number; the one at the town meeting is often phase one.
  • North Carolina Utilities Commission — docket searchSpecial contracts, large-load tariffs and rate cases are docketed here. Testimony and exhibits are public, and are usually more candid than the press release.
  • FERC eLibraryFederal filings: transmission agreements, interconnection service agreements, and co-location disputes.
  • Search the serving utility for a will-serve lettersearchThe will-serve or load-service letter is the utility's own written commitment. Ask the utility and the PUC for it by name — it is frequently the first document to exist.

Federal databases

Works anywhere, and covers the operator's record at its other sites.

  • EPA ECHO facility searchEvery federally-reported air, water and waste permit at a facility, plus its inspection and violation history. Search by address or draw a radius around the site. This project's locality centres on 36.300, -80.140 — search that point with a 5-mile radius.
  • EPA EnvirofactsThe same underlying records, queryable by county — useful for 'what else is permitted near this site' rather than one facility.
  • EPA Facility Registry ServiceResolves the shell LLC on a permit to the facility it belongs to. Worth a look when the filing name means nothing locally.

These are places to look, not evidence that anything has been filed. Links were checked on 2026-08-21; search links are queries, not records. What to ask for.

Intelligence log (31 events)
  • 2025-02-01filing
    NDA covering Project Marvel becomes effective, signed by Bessemer mayor, city attorney, and chief of staff (expires February 2027); its existence only became public in July 2026. · source

  • 2025-04-14lawsuit

  • 2025-04-24ruling

Project Red and Project Yellow In review

Hood County (Granbury area), TX · 677 ac · Filing LLC: National CRE Holdings LLC; Greenland Capital LLC

Two proposed data center campuses covering 677 acres on the grounds of the existing Wolf Hollow power generating complex in Hood County. District Judge Bryan Bufkin of the 355th Judicial District Court granted the county's plea to the jurisdiction and dismissed with prejudice the developers' suit arguing the projects were automatically approved because the county missed a 30-day statutory deadline; the judge found the submissions did not meet the state's definition of 'development plans.' Commissioners had twice delayed voting on the projects pending more disclosure and compliance with new county development regulations. Reporting identifies National CRE Holdings LLC as a Starwood Capital Group entity and Greenland Capital LLC as the owner of MARA Holdings, which already operates two bitcoin mining sites in the county.

Next step: An application is in the record. Ask the planning office for the next hearing date and request formal notice.

    State Sen. Paul Bettencourt and State Rep. Jared Patterson sent a letter to Attorney General Ken Paxton shortly before the moratorium vote urging him to investigate counties seeking data center moratoriums, arguing counties lack constitutional authority to issue them. · source
  • 2026-02-24vote
    Hood County Commissioners Court rejected a second data center moratorium proposal in a 3-2 vote with the same split; commissioners voted instead to request a formal opinion from Attorney General Ken Paxton on whether the county has legal authority to enact such a ban. · source
  • 2026-03-10vote
    Hood County Commissioners unanimously adopted amended Section One Development Permit Regulations requiring data center developers to demonstrate committed water resources, submit complete power generation concept plans, certify compliance with the Lone Star Infrastructure Protection Act, and limit building coverage to 10% of a property (down from 50%). · source
  • 2026-03-24vote
    Hood County Commissioners unanimously voted to postpone action on the Project Red and Project Yellow concept plans pending receipt of additional information; the meeting revealed MARA Holdings' connection to both developments through a joint venture with Starwood, and residents raised concerns about environmental impacts and noise from existing MARA bitcoin mining operations. · source
  • 2026-06-02coverage
    The Texas Tribune reported that Hood County faces eight proposed data center projects spanning over 7,600 acres, including the 677-acre Project Red and Project Yellow on grounds neighboring the Wolf Hollow power plants; commissioners had twice delayed voting on those two projects pending more disclosure, prompting the developers to sue claiming automatic approval. · source
  • 2026-07-15filing
    National CRE Holdings LLC and Greenland Capital LLC filed notice of appeal of Judge Bufkin's dismissal to the Second Court of Appeals. · source
  • 2026-07-15ruling
    District Judge Bryan Bufkin of the 355th Judicial District Court granted Hood County's plea to the jurisdiction and dismissed with prejudice the lawsuit by National CRE Holdings LLC and Greenland Capital LLC, ruling their concept plan submissions did not meet the statutory definition of 'development plans' that would trigger automatic approval under the 30-day deadline. · source

State environmental permits

Backup generators, water withdrawal and stormwater are permitted by the state, usually earlier and in more detail than anything filed locally.

  • Texas TCEQ — Air Permits DivisionThe program page: which permits this state requires, and the office that issues them.
  • TCEQ Central RegistrySearchable public filings — search the operator, the shell LLC on the deed, and the address.

County & town filings

The rezoning application, site plan, traffic and noise studies, staff report and every revision.

  • Search Hood County (Granbury area) planning filingssearchPlanning departments post application files under many different names. Find the department, then ask the clerk for the application number — that number unlocks everything else.
  • Search Hood County (Granbury area) property records / GISsearchThe parcel record names the buying LLC and the sale date, which is what ties an anonymous filing to an operator.

Utility & grid records

The electricity request is filed with the grid operator and the utility long before the town hears about it — and states the real load.

  • ERCOT (Texas) — interconnection queueRequested megawatts, queue position and target in-service date. The MW here is the real number; the one at the town meeting is often phase one.
  • Public Utility Commission of Texas — docket searchSpecial contracts, large-load tariffs and rate cases are docketed here. Testimony and exhibits are public, and are usually more candid than the press release.
  • FERC eLibraryFederal filings: transmission agreements, interconnection service agreements, and co-location disputes.
  • Search the serving utility for a will-serve lettersearchThe will-serve or load-service letter is the utility's own written commitment. Ask the utility and the PUC for it by name — it is frequently the first document to exist.

Federal databases

Works anywhere, and covers the operator's record at its other sites.

  • EPA ECHO facility searchEvery federally-reported air, water and waste permit at a facility, plus its inspection and violation history. Search by address or draw a radius around the site. This project's locality centres on 32.430, -97.830 — search that point with a 5-mile radius.
  • EPA EnvirofactsThe same underlying records, queryable by county — useful for 'what else is permitted near this site' rather than one facility.
  • EPA Facility Registry ServiceResolves the shell LLC on a permit to the facility it belongs to. Worth a look when the filing name means nothing locally.

These are places to look, not evidence that anything has been filed. Links were checked on 2026-08-21; search links are queries, not records. What to ask for.

Project Zora In review

Warrick County (reclaimed mine land), IN · 300 ac · Ownership not yet identified

Developer controls roughly 1,200 acres of reclaimed mine land in northern Warrick County; the preliminary concept would develop about 300 acres and leave 900 as buffer. County officials met the Project Zora development team on July 30, 2026, emphasizing no votes, commitments, or NDAs were signed and that the developer's capacity/cost claims are unverified. The end user is expected to be publicly identified by end of 2026, with no permit applications before January 2027; commissioners held an Aug 11, 2026 special meeting on data-center zoning-code amendments.

Next step: An application is in the record. Ask the planning office for the next hearing date and request formal notice.

Intelligence log (10 events)
  • 2025-12-06coverage
    Local media reported that Sourcecolo, a Utah-based data center consulting firm, was scheduled to present an informational presentation on data centers to the Warrick County Area Plan Commission on December 8, 2025; the company had already contacted CenterPoint utility about energy generation capacity, and a 'Just Say No to Data Centers' Facebook event drew nearly 80 interested attendees. · source
  • 2025-12-08hearing
    The Sourcecolo data center presentation to the Warrick County APC was postponed from December 8 to February 9, 2026, to allow board members and county officials time to conduct their own research and prepare questions; APC Executive Director Molly Barnhill said the February meeting would be informational only. · source
  • 2026-05-21hearing
    The Warrick County APC scheduled a public hearing for June 8 to discuss proposed ordinance regulations establishing definitions and regulations for small, medium, and large data centers; background noted the Sourcecolo presentation had been postponed multiple times since late 2025. · source
  • 2026-07-13hearing
    Nearly 200 residents attended a 3.5-hour Warrick County APC public hearing on a proposed data center ordinance classifying facilities as small (under 10,000 sq ft), medium (10,001-40,000 sq ft), and large (over 40,000 sq ft), with large data centers not a permitted use; the board voted 5-2 to table the ordinance for four months. · source
  • 2026-07-13moratorium
    At the same APC meeting, the board voted 4-3 to draft an additional ordinance placing a moratorium on all data center projects through December 2026, to be forwarded to the County Commissioners as a recommendation. · source
  • 2026-07-15coverage
    Wisdom 92.1 (WZDM) reported on data center opposition in Warrick County following the approximately 200-person APC hearing, noting residents' concerns about water use, noise, pollution, and loss of farmland, while proponents emphasized jobs and apprenticeship opportunities in the construction trades. · source
  • 2026-07-30announcement
    Warrick County officials and Economic Development representatives met with the Project Zora development team; no votes, commitments, or NDAs signed. Developer described control of ~1,200 acres of reclaimed mine land with ~300 acres proposed for development. · source
  • 2026-07-31announcement
    Warrick County Commissioners announced a special public meeting for August 11 at the Friedman Park Event Center in Newburgh to consider the APC's recommendation on amending the zoning code for data centers; commissioners disclosed the Project Zora developer expects to identify the end user by end of 2026 and will not submit permit applications before January 2027. · source
  • 2026-08-10hearing
    At a Monday APC meeting, Warrick County residents pushed back against Project Zora as details emerged about the proposed data center on 1,200 acres of reclaimed mine land; commissioners confirmed they refused to sign a non-disclosure agreement with the developers and that no formal application or site review had been submitted. · source
  • 2026-08-11moratorium
    Warrick County Commissioners unanimously voted to enact a 180-day moratorium pausing all data center development, stating the pause would allow time for research and regulation development; residents at the meeting expressed concerns about water usage, noise, light pollution, and wildlife disruption, with some calling for a permanent ban rather than a temporary pause. · source

Quantica Big Sky Campus In review

Broadview (Yellowstone County), MT · 1,000 MW · Operator: Quantica Infrastructure

5,000-acre campus; NorthWestern Energy committed up to 1,000 MW to Quantica as of July 2026, with Phase I construction slated for 2026.

Next step: An application is in the record. Ask the planning office for the next hearing date and request formal notice.

Source

Intelligence log (27 events)
  • 2015-01-01filing
    Invenergy requested interconnection to NorthWestern Energy's Broadview substation, the earliest step in what would become the Big Sky Campus site's grid access. · source
  • 2020-01-01financing
    Broad Reach Power purchased the Broadview interconnection project from Invenergy, with Daniel Zolnikov serving as local developer. · source
  • 2023-08-01financing
    ENGIE acquired Broad Reach Power, folding the Broadview-area power project into its portfolio ahead of the Quantica spinout. · source
  • 2024-01-01announcement
    Montana Property LLC quietly acquired roughly 5,000 acres (about eight square miles) south of Broadview, later revealed as the land assembly for Quantica's Big Sky Campus. · source
  • 2025-02-01utility
    NorthWestern Energy announced a $25-30 million transmission line project tied to the Broadview substation area, with expected completion in 2028. · source
  • 2025-07-30utility
    NorthWestern Energy signed a letter of intent to serve Quantica Infrastructure's Montana data center development, committing to a Phase 1 load of 500 MW growing to 1 GW, with initial service possible as early as 2026. · source
  • 2025-07-31hearing
    Montana's Energy and Technology Interim Committee met to study the state's power generation capacity amid data-center growth, launching studies due by September 2026. · source
  • 2025-08-01coverage
    Montana Public Radio/MEIC reported NorthWestern's proposed 1,000 MW commitment is roughly equivalent to the power used to serve 800,000 homes, more than all of NorthWestern's residential customers combined. · source
  • 2025-08-04announcement
    Quantica Infrastructure introduced Big Sky Digital Infrastructure (BSDI) as its flagship Montana development platform for the 5,000-acre Big Sky Campus, with construction planned to begin in 2026. · source
  • 2025-12-01ruling
    The Montana Public Service Commission decided to keep NorthWestern Energy's letters of intent with three data-center developers confidential as trade secrets. · source
  • 2026-01-16filing
    The Butte-Silver Bow Council of Commissioners sent a letter to the PSC advocating separate rate classifications to shield existing ratepayers from data-center-driven boom-bust risk. · source
  • 2026-02-12environmental
    AP/Montana Free Press reported Quantica does not yet hold water rights for the Broadview site and is evaluating zero-water air cooling, deep aquifer wells, treated greywater, and direct-to-chip liquid cooling. · source
  • 2026-02-20public-comment
    A coalition including Earthjustice, MEIC, NW Energy Coalition, and Honor the Earth sent a letter to the Montana PSC demanding disclosure of NorthWestern's talks with 11 additional data-center developers. · source
  • 2026-02-23report
    Daily Montanan reported NorthWestern Energy was in talks with at least 11 additional data-center entities beyond Atlas, Sabey, and Quantica, which combined could draw enough power for 1.6 million homes. · source
  • 2026-03-01utility
    Quantica's July 2025 letter of intent with NorthWestern progressed into a signed development agreement by roughly the first quarter of 2026. · source
  • 2026-03-12protest
    Broadview-area residents divided; resident Cari Olson founded Just One Montanan to push for a three-year statewide construction moratorium on data centers pending legislative action. · source
  • 2026-03-13lawsuit
    Earthjustice filed a motion before the Montana PSC on behalf of seven groups challenging the December 2025 decision keeping NorthWestern's data-center letters of intent confidential. · source
  • 2026-05-20filing
    Quantica filed interconnection applications with NorthWestern Energy seeking to expand generation capacity at the Big Sky Campus roughly seven-fold, from about 1,000 MW to 7,235 MW. · source
  • 2026-06-12filing
    Broadview resident Kassi Solberg submitted a citizen ballot initiative petition to Yellowstone County requiring two-thirds voter approval before any data center could be built or expanded. · source
  • 2026-06-17announcement
    Quantica signed an agreement with a Montana union federation covering the Big Sky Campus project, though coverage criticized it for being thin on enforceable labor details. · source
  • 2026-06-25filing
    The Yellowstone County attorney's office approved the ballot language for the citizen data-center initiative, allowing signature gathering to proceed toward the November ballot. · source
  • 2026-06-30coverage
    Daily Montanan reported on a growing citizen movement across Montana counties seeking direct voter oversight of data-center construction. · source
  • 2026-07-09hearing
    Yellowstone County commissioners held a meeting at which details of a planned lawsuit challenging the legality of the citizen data-center ballot initiative were distributed. · source
  • 2026-07-13ruling
    Yellowstone County asserted this date was the actual legal deadline for signature collection on the data-center ballot initiative, after officials said they learned of a 2025 election-statute change following contact from Quantica's attorney. · source
  • 2026-07-28filing
    Yellowstone County commissioners proposed a new policy restricting signature-gathering for citizen initiatives, amid the ongoing dispute over the data-center ballot measure. · source
  • 2026-08-03ruling
    Yellowstone County commissioners announced the true signature-gathering deadline had already passed on July 13, effectively blocking the initiative from the November ballot. · source
  • 2026-08-15ruling
    A Yellowstone County District Court judge ruled the signature-collection deadline had passed, keeping the two-thirds-voter-approval data-center initiative off the November ballot despite over 12,000 of the required 16,650 signatures collected. · source

STAK Energy North Slope Campus In review

North Slope Borough, AK · 3,000 MW · Operator: STAK Energy

$500M, up to 3GW natural-gas-powered AI data center campus on 715 leased acres ~26 mi south of Deadhorse; received preliminary state land-lease approval, construction targeted summer 2026.

Next step: An application is in the record. Ask the planning office for the next hearing date and request formal notice.

Source

Intelligence log (12 events)
  • 2025-11-01filing
    Stak Energy submitted its initial application to Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas for a 50-year state land lease (ADL 422741) covering 715.4 acres off the Dalton Highway near Milepost 390 for a natural-gas-powered AI data center campus; DNR solicited competing bids and none came in. · source
  • 2026-03-12filing
    Stak Energy filed a revised application amending its original lease submission to the Division of Oil and Gas. · source
  • 2026-05-12ruling
    Alaska DNR issued a preliminary best-interest finding for the proposed 50-year land lease to Stak Energy, granting preliminary approval for the 715-acre parcel. · source
  • 2026-05-14coverage
    Alaska Beacon broke the story of the proposed $500 million, up-to-3GW natural-gas-powered Stak Energy data center campus on the North Slope. · source
  • 2026-05-18coverage
    Anchorage Daily News expanded coverage detailing the 715-acre footprint, dry-air cooling advantage, and lack of a firm natural-gas supply deal at time of filing. · source
  • 2026-05-26coverage
    Alaska Public Media reported on the proposal, noting Stak Energy Alaska roots and staffing plans. · source
  • 2026-05-28report
    Northern Alaska Environmental Center published an analysis of the lease documents identifying unresolved risks: incomplete wetland delineation, no permafrost thermal modeling, no bird/caribou surveys, undisclosed lease financial terms, and estimated gas consumption of 128-183 billion cubic feet per year. · source
  • 2026-06-01environmental
    The Alaska Center publicized environmental concerns including potential heat-island warming effects extending up to 6.2 miles, the need for 7 million cubic yards of gravel to raise the site 5-7 feet, and fuel consumption potentially exceeding twice urban Alaska electrical generation; urged residents to file public comments. · source
  • 2026-06-15public-comment
    Original public comment deadline on the DNR preliminary best-interest decision for the Stak Energy lease. · source
  • 2026-07-03protest
    Coverage reported Alaskans had flooded the state comment docket with opposition, including submissions reading "HELL NO! To ANY DATA CENTERS" and "NO AI," ahead of the extended comment deadline. · source
  • 2026-07-07report
    Anchorage Daily News reported more than 500 public comments submitted to DNR, with fewer than a dozen supporting the project and the vast majority opposed; Stak Energy characterized most as form letters. · source
  • 2026-07-17public-comment
    Extended deadline (4:30 p.m.) for public comments on the proposed 50-year land lease; DNR said it would assess comments before issuing a final lease decision. · source

  • PJM Interconnection (Mid-Atlantic, Ohio Valley) — interconnection queueRequested megawatts, queue position and target in-service date. The MW here is the real number; the one at the town meeting is often phase one.
  • Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission — docket searchSpecial contracts, large-load tariffs and rate cases are docketed here. Testimony and exhibits are public, and are usually more candid than the press release.
  • FERC eLibraryFederal filings: transmission agreements, interconnection service agreements, and co-location disputes.
  • Search the serving utility for a will-serve lettersearchThe will-serve or load-service letter is the utility's own written commitment. Ask the utility and the PUC for it by name — it is frequently the first document to exist.

Federal databases

Works anywhere, and covers the operator's record at its other sites.

  • EPA ECHO facility searchEvery federally-reported air, water and waste permit at a facility, plus its inspection and violation history. Search by address or draw a radius around the site. This project's locality centres on 40.538, -79.790 — search that point with a 5-mile radius.
  • EPA EnvirofactsThe same underlying records, queryable by county — useful for 'what else is permitted near this site' rather than one facility.
  • EPA Facility Registry ServiceResolves the shell LLC on a permit to the facility it belongs to. Worth a look when the filing name means nothing locally.

These are places to look, not evidence that anything has been filed. Links were checked on 2026-08-21; search links are queries, not records. What to ask for.

Stratos In review

Box Elder County (near Brigham City), UT · 1,100 MW · Operator: O'Leary Digital

O'Leary Digital, chaired by Kevin O'Leary, proposes the Stratos campus in unincorporated Box Elder County near Brigham City: eleven 100 MW data center buildings plus a 7.5-9 GW natural gas plant and a 500 MW solar array on roughly 40,000 acres across three sites. Renderings were released 2026-05-19; the county commission approved an interlocal agreement with the Military Installation Development Authority in early May 2026. State environmental permitting could take about two years, with a 30-day public comment period and hearing required, and over 40 protests have been filed on its water rights application.

Next step: An application is in the record. Ask the planning office for the next hearing date and request formal notice.

Source
read 2026-08-14

Intelligence log (15 events)
  • 2026-04-24vote
    MIDA's board of directors approved four resolutions and a tax ordinance creating the Stratos Project Area, before Box Elder County had formally consented; critics later alleged MIDA also signed a development agreement the same morning. · source
  • 2026-05-04vote
    Box Elder County Commission approved Resolutions 26-11 and 26-12 consenting to the MIDA Stratos Project Area and an interlocal agreement, at a contentious meeting at the county fairgrounds in Tremonton with hundreds of opponents present and sheriff's deputies controlling the crowd. · source
  • 2026-05-07withdrawal
    The holder of an 1904-vintage water right withdrew a change application seeking to convert 1,900 acre-feet from agricultural to industrial use for the Stratos project, after more than 3,700 formal protests were filed at $15 each; the developer stated it fully intends to refile. · source
  • 2026-05-12coverage
    Utah House Speaker Mike Schultz said he did not attend the meeting Kevin O'Leary described on Fox News and only learned of the project in early April 2026; the Deseret News reported the project's estimated cost exceeds $100 billion. · source
  • 2026-05-14protest
    Approximately 400 to 500 people rallied at the Utah Capitol against the Stratos project, delivering an opposition letter signed by over 7,500 people calling on Governor Cox, House Speaker Schultz, and Senate President Adams to order independent water and fiscal studies. · source
  • 2026-05-18environmental
    Grist reported the project would raise Utah's carbon emissions by 64 percent and that a physics professor calculated 16 gigawatts of waste heat could spike Hansel Valley nighttime temperatures by as much as 28 degrees Fahrenheit. · source
  • 2026-05-19announcement
    O'Leary Digital released renderings of the proposed Stratos campus in Box Elder County; state environmental approvals were estimated at roughly two years, with air monitoring required for one year before a permit application. · source
  • 2026-05-23protest
    Hundreds of Utahns rallied at the state Capitol a second time demanding a halt to the Box Elder data center plan, calling on state leaders to protect water, air, and land. · source
  • 2026-05-28denial
    Box Elder County Attorney Stephen Hadfield rejected three referendum applications challenging the May 4 commission vote, ruling the resolutions were irrevocable administrative actions rather than newly created laws and thus not referable to voters. · source
  • 2026-05-28coverage
    Governor Spencer Cox declared the Stratos project will 'never' run solely on natural gas, stating the first phase would use gas but subsequent phases should use nuclear, geothermal, and solar power. · source
  • 2026-06-03lawsuit
    Alliance for a Better Utah and five Box Elder County residents filed suit in Utah's 3rd District Court challenging MIDA's constitutionality and seeking to void the Stratos approval, also alleging Senate President Adams had a conflict of interest from a $135,000 PAC donation. · source
  • 2026-06-03lawsuit
    Box Elder Accountability Referendum (BEAR) filed an appeal in Utah 1st District Court in Brigham City challenging the county attorney's rejection of referendum applications on Resolutions 26-11 and 26-12, arguing the approvals were legislative acts subject to voter referendum. · source
  • 2026-06-04announcement
    O'Leary agreed to cut the project area from roughly 40,000 acres to 20,000 acres, removing the Locomotive Springs and I-84 parcels and keeping only the Hansel Valley parcel, with 10,000 acres designated as open space. · source
  • 2026-06-10moratorium
    Box Elder County commissioners unanimously approved a 180-day moratorium on new data centers and power plants on unincorporated land, but explicitly exempted the Stratos project whose land-use authority had been transferred to MIDA for 50 years. · source
  • 2026-07-29coverage
    Kevin O'Leary said design work on the Stratos data center is 'full steam ahead' while MIDA remains on 'pause' awaiting permit requests for the project. · source

Urbana Technology Hub In review

Urbana (Champaign County), OH · 230 ac · Operator: Thor Equities · Owner: Thor Equities · Filing LLC: Urbana Investment Group LLC

Thor Equities assembled approximately 230 acres near Ohio 55 and US 68 for a 460,000 sq ft, $1B+ data center campus called the Urbana Technology Hub. A site plan application was submitted February 13 but deemed incomplete by city staff. The BZA unanimously denied Thor's appeal. The city council then adopted new zoning codes removing data centers as a permitted use in the M-1 manufacturing district. Thor Equities filed a federal lawsuit in the US District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. A charter amendment petition and mayor recall effort are also underway.

Next step: Application filed. Ask the planning office for the hearing date and request formal notice.

Meta Lebanon / LEAP Data Center Campus Proposed

Boone County, IN · 1,000 MW · Operator: Meta · Tenant: Meta

1500-acre, 1GW, $10B+ Meta campus at the LEAP Lebanon Innovation District. Multiple sources (WISH-TV, WRTV, Data Center Dynamics, IndyStar) place this site on land annexed into the City of Lebanon as part of the state-sponsored LEAP district -- NOT unincorporated Boone County and NOT the Town of Advance. This conflicts with the task baseline description citing the Town of Advance; flagging for the tracker maintainer to reconcile (see research_notes). Either way, all reporting agrees this project is exempt from the county's unincorporated-land moratorium. First proposed publicly around Nov 2024 (~$800M), then expanded to the current $10B/1GW scope announced Feb 2026; groundbreaking construction reported ongoing through mid-2026 with resident complaints about light/noise pollution.

Recore Digital AI data center inquiry Rumored

Grant County, IN · — · Operator: Recore Digital

An inquiry, not an application. Recore Digital approached the Grant County Area Plan Commission in July 2026 about converting an existing cryptocurrency mining operation in the county into what it describes as a 'quiet, permanent AI Data Center'. The county's 24-month moratorium (Ordinance 4-2026) bars improvement-location permits for data centers in unincorporated areas until March 2028 or until the APC's data center ordinance is adopted, so the live question is what that ordinance will require; a seven-member subcommittee (four APC members, three residents) finished its first review of the draft in August 2026. Site, size, power and water figures have not been published. Coordinates are the county centroid.

Next step: Rumored only. Confirm with the planning office and file a records request to pin down what is real.

Source
read 2026-09-02

Intelligence log (5 events)
  • 2025-12-01meeting
    Grant County Area Plan Commission began outlining a data center ordinance — annual energy and water reporting, client-category disclosure, infrastructure offsets, and rules for standby diesel generators and cooling noise were among the items discussed (minutes on the county's APC minutes server; secondary account at citizenportal.ai). · source
  • 2026-03-16moratorium
    Board of Commissioners adopted Ordinance 4-2026, a 24-month moratorium on data center improvement-location permits in unincorporated Grant County, 3-0, after county attorney Martin Harker read it aloud. · source
  • 2026-07-11proposal
    Chronicle-Tribune reported that Recore Digital wants to bring a 'quiet, permanent AI Data Center' to Grant County and had approached the Area Plan Commission; the APC's data center subcommittee is seven volunteers — four commission members and three from the public. · source
  • 2026-07-25coverage
    Chronicle-Tribune opinion column (Tom Marine) described the inquiry as a proposal to convert an existing cryptocurrency mining operation and argued the first applicant should not write the county's rulebook. · source
  • 2026-08-08meeting
    The APC's data center subcommittee met to complete its initial review of the draft data center ordinance; the Chronicle-Tribune described the county as 'one step closer to finalizing a data center ordinance'. · source

1155 Powers Ferry Place data center (Prime Storage site) Approved

Marietta (Cobb County), GA · 18 MW · Owner: Prime Group Holdings

Marietta City Council voted 5-2 on Aug 12, 2026 to approve rezoning for an 18 MW, 90,000 sq ft data center at Prime Storage's ~11-acre Powers Ferry Place property near I-75 and Delk Road — the city's second data center. Conditions include silencers on coolers/generators, an independent sound study, no connection to municipal water, and Prime Storage agreeing not to build data centers at its other Marietta sites. The application predated the six-month moratorium the council passed July 8.

Next step: Approved — pivot from stopping it to a binding CBA: enforceable caps on noise, water and cost, plus a community benefit.

Antelope Data Campus (Project Antelope) Approved

Iron County (near Cedar City), UT · 640 ac · Filing LLC: Pronghorn Development LLC

Iron County Planning Commission unanimously approved a conditional use permit on 2026-06-04 for Pronghorn Development LLC's five-building campus (up to 6.75M sq ft, with an on-site natural gas plant of up to 1.5 GW) on 640 acres along Antelope Springs Road, about 8 miles west of Cedar City, with 62 conditions covering water rights, wastewater, noise, lighting and site restoration.   • 2025-01-01rezoning

  • 2026-04-08vote

State environmental permits

Backup generators, water withdrawal and stormwater are permitted by the state, usually earlier and in more detail than anything filed locally.

  • Texas TCEQ — Air Permits DivisionThe program page: which permits this state requires, and the office that issues them.
  • TCEQ Central RegistrySearchable public filings — search the operator, the shell LLC on the deed, and the address.

County & town filings

The rezoning application, site plan, traffic and noise studies, staff report and every revision.

  • Search Fort Worth planning filingssearchPlanning departments post application files under many different names. Find the department, then ask the clerk for the application number — that number unlocks everything else.
  • Search Fort Worth property records / GISsearchThe parcel record names the buying LLC and the sale date, which is what ties an anonymous filing to an operator.

Utility & grid records

The electricity request is filed with the grid operator and the utility long before the town hears about it — and states the real load.

  • ERCOT (Texas) — interconnection queueRequested megawatts, queue position and target in-service date. The MW here is the real number; the one at the town meeting is often phase one.
  • Public Utility Commission of Texas — docket searchSpecial contracts, large-load tariffs and rate cases are docketed here. Testimony and exhibits are public, and are usually more candid than the press release.
  • FERC eLibraryFederal filings: transmission agreements, interconnection service agreements, and co-location disputes.
  • Search the serving utility for a will-serve lettersearchThe will-serve or load-service letter is the utility's own written commitment. Ask the utility and the PUC for it by name — it is frequently the first document to exist.

Federal databases

Works anywhere, and covers the operator's record at its other sites.

  • EPA ECHO facility searchEvery federally-reported air, water and waste permit at a facility, plus its inspection and violation history. Search by address or draw a radius around the site.
  • EPA EnvirofactsThe same underlying records, queryable by county — useful for 'what else is permitted near this site' rather than one facility.
  • EPA Facility Registry ServiceResolves the shell LLC on a permit to the facility it belongs to. Worth a look when the filing name means nothing locally.

These are places to look, not evidence that anything has been filed. Links were checked on 2026-08-21; search links are queries, not records. What to ask for.

Compass Datacenters Red Oak campus Approved

Red Oak (Ellis County), TX · 830 ac · Operator: Compass Datacenters

Red Oak City Council voted 4-1 to rezone ~830 acres of agricultural land ~20 miles south of Dallas to a planned development for a Compass data center campus of nearly a dozen buildings plus substations, after a marathon May 11 meeting that ran past midnight with 150+ residents present and ~1,600 petition signatures against; the planning and zoning board had recommended denial in late April. Conditions include lighting shields, decibel limits, a cryptocurrency-mining ban, closed-loop cooling with no city water draw, and $72 million in electric grid reinforcements; a 10-year, $2.82 million tax abatement passed on a separate 4-1 vote.

DataOne USA / Nebius Vineland (Microsoft) Approved

Vineland, NJ · 300 MW · Operator: Nebius · Owner: Nebius · Tenant: Microsoft · Filing LLC: NEP Real Estate of Vineland NJ Urban Renewal LLC; applicant changed to DataOne USA LLC in July 2025

South Jersey's largest data center: 2,647,628 sq ft approved in four phases over twelve years off South Lincoln and Sheridan avenues, built by DataOne USA for Nebius, whose GPU capacity here is contracted to Microsoft under a $17.4B five-year deal. Phase one was already operating before an environmental impact statement was published (Feb 2026). Three live disputes: NOISE - a county noise violation in March 2026 and a federal nuisance class action that was voluntarily dismissed on jurisdictional grounds in June 2026, not on the merits; POWER - the board approved 300 MW of behind-the-meter Bloom Energy fuel cells plus a 1.5-million-gallon LNG tank on Aug 17, 2026, after two city stop-work orders for building that equipment without permits; AIR - NJDEP says it has issued no permits and has no applications under review for power generators at the site, while thermal drone imagery published Aug 27, 2026 showed at least 45 of 62 gas generators running. Water figures conflict: the applicant's Aug 2026 case put annual use near 8 million gallons; a 2024 Vineland water department estimate cited by opponents put it above 1.1 billion gallons a year. Vineland has no data center moratorium; neighbouring Millville banned them outright in May 2026.

Next step: Approved — pivot from stopping it to a binding CBA: enforceable caps on noise, water and cost, plus a community benefit.

State environmental permits

Backup generators, water withdrawal and stormwater are permitted by the state, usually earlier and in more detail than anything filed locally.

  • Virginia DEQThe program page: which permits this state requires, and the office that issues them.
  • Search Virginia DEQ for this projectsearchThis state publishes no searchable permit database, so a written records request to the agency is the reliable route. Use this search only to find the right office.

County & town filings

The rezoning application, site plan, traffic and noise studies, staff report and every revision.

  • Search Louisa County (Shannon Hill) planning filingssearchPlanning departments post application files under many different names. Find the department, then ask the clerk for the application number — that number unlocks everything else.
  • Search Louisa County (Shannon Hill) property records / GISsearchThe parcel record names the buying LLC and the sale date, which is what ties an anonymous filing to an operator.

Utility & grid records

The electricity request is filed with the grid operator and the utility long before the town hears about it — and states the real load.

  • PJM Interconnection (Mid-Atlantic, Ohio Valley) — interconnection queueRequested megawatts, queue position and target in-service date. The MW here is the real number; the one at the town meeting is often phase one.
  • Virginia State Corporation Commission — docket searchSpecial contracts, large-load tariffs and rate cases are docketed here. Testimony and exhibits are public, and are usually more candid than the press release.
  • FERC eLibraryFederal filings: transmission agreements, interconnection service agreements, and co-location disputes.
  • Search the serving utility for a will-serve lettersearchThe will-serve or load-service letter is the utility's own written commitment. Ask the utility and the PUC for it by name — it is frequently the first document to exist.

Federal databases

Works anywhere, and covers the operator's record at its other sites.

  • EPA ECHO facility searchEvery federally-reported air, water and waste permit at a facility, plus its inspection and violation history. Search by address or draw a radius around the site. This project's locality centres on 37.870, -78.080 — search that point with a 5-mile radius.
  • EPA EnvirofactsThe same underlying records, queryable by county — useful for 'what else is permitted near this site' rather than one facility.
  • EPA Facility Registry ServiceResolves the shell LLC on a permit to the facility it belongs to. Worth a look when the filing name means nothing locally.
